Read a field with `view.text(record, field)`, its versions with `view.text_versions(record, field)` and who wrote what with `view.authorship(record, field)`; write one of your own with `writer.set_text` in an op, or propose the core ops `text.edit` and `text.propose` from an action. The `text_version` record and the text ops are under Core records and Core ops.

## Working copies

Working copies (design 5.0): long text handed out as a file for the person's own tool, and taken back.

Handing out runs the format's `hand_out` on a version, keeps the file through the file channel and records what went out (the version, the file's hash). Taking back runs `take_back` on the returned file with the handed-out version's text and files the result as a `text.propose` made from that version, so the review is three-way when the text moved on; whatever couldn't be mapped is kept beside the proposal. A file that comes back unchanged proposes nothing, and a file that wouldn't read back to the text it was made from isn't handed out. All of it is deterministic: no AI, nothing to estimate or pay for.

Registered with `registrar.working_copy` (see Registering). The `working_copy` record is under Core records.

### TakeBack

What a working-copy format read back from a file: the whole text, and anything it couldn't map (a comment, a style it doesn't know), in plain words, shown beside the proposal and never dropped silently.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | str | required |
| `unmapped` | list[str] | `[]` |

### WorkingCopyContext

What a working-copy format sees: the record, the field, the version handed out, the language, the plugin's settings and its data files.

## Programs

Outside programs a plugin declares in `requires.tools` (design 3.2, 3.5), run without a shell in a fresh folder.

Where a program is found is set per computer in `.cockpit/tools.yaml`, which is never synced:

```
checker: {command: [/opt/checker/bin/run, --strict], env: {CHECKER_HOME: /opt/checker}}
renderer: /usr/local/bin/renderer
```

A tool missing from that file is looked up on the PATH by its name. Each declared tool is probed once per process: its probe command runs, and the first version number in its output is compared with the declared minimum.

A run writes the given files into a temporary folder, runs the program there with a timeout and a minimal environment, and returns its exit code, output and the files it wrote that match the call's `collect` patterns, within size caps. The folder is deleted afterwards. Everything a program returns is untrusted material.

### `context.tools`

What a plugin sees: only the tools its manifest declares, each probed before it runs. Every run is recorded.

#### `context.tools.available(name: str) -> bool`

Whether a declared program is installed on this computer and new enough (probed once per run of the host).

#### `context.tools.run(name: str, args: Sequence[str], files: Mapping[str, bytes] | None = None, timeout: float | None = None, *, collect: Sequence[str] = (), max_file_mb: float | None = None, max_total_mb: float | None = None) -> ToolResult`

Run a declared tool. `files` are written to a fresh working folder first, by relative path; `collect` patterns return files the program wrote there. Caps and the timeout may be lowered, never raised.

### ToolResult

How a program run ended and what it returned. A run that timed out has `timed_out` set and returncode -1; `output_cut` says stdout or stderr was longer than the cap and was cut there; `files` are the collected files by path inside the working folder; `omitted` lists matched files not returned, as {name, size, reason}.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `returncode` | int | required |
| `stdout` | str | required |
| `stderr` | str | required |
| `timed_out` | bool | `False` |
| `output_cut` | bool | `False` |
| `files` | dict[str, bytes] | `{}` |
| `omitted` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` |
| `seconds` | float | `0.0` |

## Publishing a pack

Checking a pack before it is published: `cockpit pack check <plugin folder> [--entry <catalog entry>]`.

Publishing a pack (the process every plugin repository follows; the catalog's PUBLISHING.md says the same):

1. **Release it in its own repository.** Raise the version in `plugin.yaml` (and the package's own metadata), say what changed, run its tests, tag the release, and let its own checks build the package from the tag.

2. **Write its catalog entry** as `catalog/pack.yaml` in that repository, in the catalog's format (the catalog repository's README): `provides` and `requires` copied exactly from `plugin.yaml`, its price, how to get it, and its typical AI jobs.

3. **Check it:** `cockpit pack check <its plugin folder> --entry catalog/pack.yaml`, with the host at the version the pack declares. Every line must pass. A pack whose plugins share a helper package from the same distribution is checked installed: install the built package beside the host and name the plugin instead of its folder (`cockpit pack check <plugin name> --entry catalog/pack.yaml`). An entry file listing several packs is matched to the plugin by its id.

4. **Ask for it to be published:** add a "Publish request" to its `docs/host-questions.md` (the pack, the version and tag, what changed, the check's output, and whether the owner has said it may be listed publicly) and tell the host's session. A plugin repository never writes to the catalog itself.

5. **The host verifies and proposes:** the host's session checks the release again itself (the same check, the pack's tests, a run in the demo sandbox) and opens a pull request on the catalog with the entry, saying what the pack adds, reaches and keeps, and what changed in what it asks for since its last listing.

6. **The owner decides:** the pack is listed only once the owner has said it may be, and the pull request is merged (by the owner, or by the host's session when the owner has handed it that). Updates follow the same path.

A pack that ships files its source control ignores (an app registration written by the release build, say) builds its wheel straight from the checkout: a wheel built from the source archive leaves such files out. Check the built package holds them before publishing.

The check reports each finding in plain words and passes only when every one does.

## Wording

A plugin's wording files (`provides.wording`) may set these keys for identifiers in its own namespace; the screens read nothing else from them. The workspace's `ui.wording` overrides any of them.

| Key | What it names |
|---|---|
| `task.{task kind}` | What a kind of AI work is called (set from the task kind's label unless the file sets it). |
| `stages.group.{record kind}` | The heading for a kind of record on the Stages screen. |
| `op.{op}` | What an op is called in What changed and on reviews. |
| `setup_step.{setup step}` | A setup step's title in the setup guide (instead of its label). |
| `setup_step.{setup step}.explanation` | A setup step's explanation in the setup guide. |
| `welcome.skip.{setup step}` | The words on a setup step's Skip button. |

## Connectors

What `registrar.connector`'s `poll` returns and raises.

### SourceItem

One thing a source holds. `key`: stable within the source (a message or event id), so the same thing read again is compared with what was seen. `title`: one line naming it. `text`: everything the assistant should read about it now, as plain text; a change is a change in this text. `author`: who changed it last, as the service names them (triage rules compare it with `workspace.our_accounts`). `changed_at`: when, as the service says it. `link`: where the person can open it. `event` or `message` (at most one): what it is, for a calendar item or a mail item, so Today can show the day's agenda and what came in; the text still says everything the assistant reads. `files`: the files it carries (attachments), which the core reads and adds to the text.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | str | required |
| `title` | str | required |
| `text` | str | required |
| `author` | str \| None | `None` |
| `changed_at` | str \| None | `None` |
| `link` | str \| None | `None` |
| `event` | EventDetails \| None | `None` |
| `message` | MessageDetails \| None | `None` |
| `files` | tuple[ItemFile, ...] | `()` |

### ItemFile

A file an item carries (a mail's attachment, a document in a folder). `name`: its file name. `media_type`: its type as the service says it; when that is missing or generic, the name's ending decides. `data`: its bytes. The core reads it as text with its readers (a plugin's reader for the type first), cuts the text at the configured size and adds it to the item's text, so a connector never parses a file and hands over what it has.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required |
| `media_type` | str | required |
| `data` | bytes | required |

### EventDetails

What a calendar item is, for the day's agenda. `start` and `end`: ISO 8601 date-times with their offset (`2026-03-02T09:30:00+01:00` or `...Z`), or plain dates (`2026-03-02`) with `all_day`; an all-day `end` is the day after the last day, as calendars write it. `where`: the place or the meeting address, as the service says. `cancelled`: the organizer called it off. `repeats`: the repeat rule as the service wrote it, for an item that stands for a series the connector didn't expand into its occurrences (the agenda can't place those).

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | str | required |
| `end` | str \| None | `None` |
| `all_day` | bool | `False` |
| `where` | str \| None | `None` |
| `cancelled` | bool | `False` |
| `repeats` | str \| None | `None` |

### MessageDetails

What a mail item is, for the day's inbox. `sender`: who it is from, as the service names them, with the address in angle brackets when it has one (`Name <name@example.com>`), which sender rules read. `received`: an ISO 8601 date-time with its offset. `unread`: whether the person hasn't opened it yet, when the service says. `bulk`: whether the message says it was sent to many (it has a list-unsubscribe header, or a bulk or list precedence), None when the connector can't tell. `categories`: the service's own categories or labels for it, as read and in lower case (promotions, social, say); empty when it has none or doesn't say. `participants`: everyone else on the message (the people it was sent to, and those copied), each as the service names them, with the address in angle brackets when it has one; empty when there are none or the service doesn't say. A first name in the text means the person of that name who is on the message.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `sender` | str \| None | `None` |
| `received` | str \| None | `None` |
| `unread` | bool \| None | `None` |
| `bulk` | bool \| None | `None` |
| `categories` | tuple[str, ...] | `()` |
| `participants` | tuple[str, ...] | `()` |

### Poll

What a source holds now. `items`: what it lists. `complete`: True when the list is everything, so an item missing from it is gone; False when it is only what changed since `state`. `removed`: keys the service says are gone, for a read that lists only changes (handed in like an item missing from a complete read, when the source reports removals). `state`: kept and given back on the next read (a change marker, say); a read that fails keeps the state of the last read that worked.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | list[SourceItem] | required |
| `state` | dict[str, Any] | `{}` |
| `complete` | bool | `True` |
| `removed` | list[str] | `[]` |

### ConnectorError

Why a read failed. `kind`: auth (sign in again), no_access, not_found, outage (the service is failing), offline (no network here: never counted as a failure), or throttled (the service asked to wait: `retry_after` seconds; the source isn't read again before then, and it isn't counted as a failure). When the web client raised it from an answer, `status`, `headers` and `body` (its text, at most 20 KB) are the service's own, and `json()` parses the body, so a connector can read the service's error code and raise a better kind itself.

### Testing a connector: `engine.plugin_api.testing`

Testing a plugin: part of the plugin API, for plugins' own tests. A connector without a network (`connector_context`, `read`), and everything else in a throwaway workspace (`plugin_workspace`).

```
from engine.plugin_api.testing import Reply, connector_context, read
```

```
def service(asked):
    if asked.path == "/v1/changes":
        return Reply(json={"items": [...], "next": "m2"})
    return Reply(status=404)
```

```
context = connector_context(service, network=["api.example.com"], secrets={"client-id": "x"},
                            tokens={"myplugin/account": "token"})
poll = read(my_poll, MySettings(), {}, context)
```

`service(asked)` answers every request the connector makes through `context.web`: `asked` has the method, url, path (decoded; `raw_path` as sent), query (a dict of lists, blank values kept; `param(name)` gives the first value), headers and body (text, and `form` / `json()` parsed). A `Reply()` with neither `json` nor `text` has an empty body; answer `Reply(json={})` for a service that answers an empty JSON object. Only hosts in `network` are reached, over HTTPS, as in the app. `secrets` answers `context.secret(name)` and records `context.keep_secret`; `tokens` answers `context.access_token(name)`, and a sign-in missing from it raises `ConnectorError("auth")` as an expired sign-in does; `granted` answers `context.granted(name)` with each sign-in's allowed scopes (left out, `context.granted` is None, as for a connector of a plugin with no sign-ins). `read` runs `poll` and checks its answer the way the watcher does.

#### `connector_context(service: 'Callable[[Asked], Reply]', *, network: 'list[str]', secrets: 'dict[str, str] | None' = None, tokens: 'dict[str, str] | None' = None, granted: 'dict[str, set[str]] | None' = None, workspace_root: 'Path | str' = '.') -> 'ConnectorContext'`

A connector's context whose web client is answered by `service`. `kept` secrets land in `secrets`.

#### `read(poll: 'Callable[..., Poll]', settings: 'Any', state: 'dict[str, Any] | None', context: 'ConnectorContext') -> 'Poll'`

Run a connector's `poll` and check its answer as the watcher does. A ConnectorError passes through.

#### Reply and Asked

An answer: a status, and a JSON value or text, with headers (a Retry-After, say). One request a connector made.

### Testing everything else: `plugin_workspace`

#### `plugin_workspace(*folders: 'str | Path', settings: 'dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None' = None, root: 'str | Path | None' = None, from_saved: 'SavedWorkspace | None' = None, require_started: 'bool' = True) -> 'Any'`

A throwaway workspace with these plugins loaded (a plugin folder holding plugin.yaml, or an installed plugin's name), with `settings` per plugin as its settings file. A context manager: the workspace is made in `root` (a pytest `tmp_path`, say) or a temporary folder, and closed after. A plugin folder is linked into the workspace (copied where links aren't allowed), so a temporary copy of a folder works as well as the real one.

`from_saved` starts from a fresh copy of a workspace saved with `ws.save(path)` (then `folders` and `settings` are those it was saved with). A plugin that doesn't start raises `PluginDidNotStart` (with `plugin` and `reason`); `require_started=False` opens the workspace anyway, to look at `ws.status()`.

```
with plugin_workspace(PLUGIN_FOLDER, root=tmp_path) as ws:
    done = ws.apply([{"op": "myplugin/add", "title": "One"}])
    assert done.status == "applied"
```

A throwaway workspace (the fictional demo's data) with the plugins loaded, for a plugin's own tests. Use it through `plugin_workspace(...)`. Everything here goes through the same paths as the app: the applier, the dispatcher with a scripted answer, person actions, events, stage moves and the synced folder's layout.

Its attributes: `root` (the workspace folder), `plugins` (the names of the plugins given, in order) and `cfg` (the workspace's settings as loaded). `store` and `ws` are the host's own objects: reach them only where no method here covers a test, since they change with the host.

#### `ws.status(plugin: str | None = None) -> PluginState`

A plugin's status (the first plugin given, unless named), whether it started or not.

#### `ws.registered(plugin: str | None = None) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]`

What a plugin registered, by kind, read-only: {"sign_ins": {name: its declaration}, "connectors": ..., "triage_matchers", "setup_steps", "actions", "tasks", "ops", "records", "panels", "today", "jobs", "stage_checks", "file_kinds", "lints", "extractors", "scorers"}. Empty kinds are left out. A started plugin only.

#### `ws.save(path: str | Path) -> SavedWorkspace`

Save this workspace as it is now (records, settings, the plugins linked in), so other tests start from fresh copies of it with `plugin_workspace(..., from_saved=saved)` instead of building it again.

#### `ws.view(plugin: str | None = None) -> Any`

A ReadView as the plugin sees it (the first plugin given, unless named).

#### `ws.apply(ops: list[dict[str, Any]], *, summary: str = 'Test', as_person: bool = True, trusted: bool = True) -> Outcome`

Apply ops as the person (their own change, applied at once) or as the assistant (checked by validators and lints first, `trusted=False` for work from outside content), and say what became of each.

#### `ws.ask(task: str, *, answer: Any, about: tuple[str, str] | None = None, part: dict[str, Any] | None = None, note: str = '') -> AskResult`

Run a task kind with a scripted answer, through the dispatcher: the packet, the checks, the fix round and the review. `answer` is the answer's text, a dict (sent as JSON) or a function of the run's task, whose `request` carries the fix round's feedback, so it can answer differently each round.

#### `ws.action(name: str, target: Any = None, choices: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> ActionResult`

Run a person action on a record (a Stored, or (kind, id)) or the workspace, and get its proposal.

#### `ws.emit(event: str, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]`

Raise an event as the core would and return the work the handlers queued: one dict per new request (`task`, `about`, `note`, `state`).

#### `ws.move_stage(record: Any, to: str) -> Outcome`

Move a record to a stage as the person would; a refusal (an entry check failing) raises StoreError.

#### `ws.stage_status(record: Any) -> Any`

#### `ws.folder() -> dict[str, bytes]`

The files the synced folder would hold now, by path, as the core writes them (the plugin's layout, its generated files and the core's own).

#### `ws.close() -> None`

#### Outcome

What became of a changeset: its id, its `status` (applied, held, rejected) and one entry per op (`op`, `status` applied/held/refused, `reason`). `refused` lists the reasons of the refused ops; `problems` are those of the changeset as a whole.

#### AskResult

A run of a task kind: the request's `state` (review: the answer waits for the person; needs_you: it was held, with `waiting` saying why) and the `outcome` of its changeset, when there is one.

#### ActionResult

A person action's proposal as the review shows it: `summary`, `ops`, `notes`, `items`, `requests` and `problems` (why ops would be refused if applied now). `apply(kept=...)` applies it as the person would.

#### PluginState

A plugin's status as the host keeps it: `state` (enabled, disabled, off), the `reason` it is off, `notes` (problems it was told about) and its declared programs' `tools` status.

#### SavedWorkspace

A workspace saved with `ws.save()`, to start tests from fresh copies of: `plugin_workspace(..., from_saved=saved)`.

#### PluginDidNotStart

A plugin given to `plugin_workspace` didn't start: `plugin` names it and `reason` says why, as its status on the Add-ons screen would.

## Errors

| Error | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `StoreError` | A write can't be made as asked. |
| `NeedsPerson` | An op set a value only the person may set; the host holds it for the person instead of applying it. |
| `PluginMisuse` | The plugin broke its contract (reached outside its scope); the host disables it for the run. |
| `ToolError` | A run that can't start: an undeclared or missing tool, or a bad file name or pattern. |

## Settings that limit plugins

In the workspace's `config/workspace.yaml`; the person can change them.

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace.plugins.enabled` | list[str] | `[]` | Plugins enabled in this workspace, by name. |
| `workspace.plugins.actions` | ActionSettings | see below | How person actions from plugins are reviewed. |
| `workspace.plugins.actions.keep_minutes` | float | `60` | How long a reviewed proposal waits for the person's go. |
| `workspace.plugins.actions.preview_mb` | float | `5` | Largest single preview an action may show, in MB. |
| `workspace.plugins.actions.max_previews` | int | `20` | Most previews one action may show. |
| `workspace.plugins.actions.max_items` | int | `2000` | Most items one action may offer to keep or drop (a long file gives many). |
| `workspace.plugins.actions.max_requests` | int | `100` | Most pieces of follow-up work one action may queue for the assistant at once. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools` | ToolSettings | see below | Limits on the outside programs plugins run (where they are found is set per computer, not here). |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.timeout_seconds` | float | `120` | How long a plugin's program may run if it sets no limit. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.max_timeout_seconds` | float | `1800` | The longest any program may run; plugins can't ask more. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.probe_timeout_seconds` | float | `10` | How long a program's version check may take. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.output_kb` | int | `512` | How much of a program's output and error stream is kept, in KB. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.collect_file_mb` | float | `25` | Largest file a program wrote that is returned to the plugin. |
| `workspace.plugins.tools.collect_total_mb` | float | `100` | Most a program's returned files may add up to, in MB. |
| `workspace.plugins.jobs` | dict[str, JobSettings] | see below | Plugins' scheduled work, by job name: on or off, and how often. |
| `workspace.plugins.jobs.enabled` | bool | `True` | Off: the job doesn't run. |
| `workspace.plugins.jobs.every_minutes` | int \| None | `None` | How often it runs; unset means the plugin's default. |
| `workspace.plugins.secrets` | dict[str, dict[str, str]] | `{}` | Each plugin's secrets, by plugin then secret name, as references (env:NAME or file:/path), never the secret itself. |
| `workspace.plugins.failures_before_off` | int | `3` | How many times in a row a plugin's Today lines, interface items, event handler or job may fail before the plugin is turned off; each failure is noted on the plugin. |
| `workspace.plugins.catalog` | CatalogSettings | see below | Where the Add-ons screen finds packs to tell you about. |
| `workspace.plugins.catalog.enabled` | bool | `True` | Show the packs catalog feeds list on the Add-ons screen. |
| `workspace.plugins.catalog.shipped_feed` | bool | `True` | Include the catalog feed this build of the app came with, if any. |
| `workspace.plugins.catalog.feeds` | list[str] | `[]` | More catalog feeds to read, as https addresses (a team's own, say). |
| `workspace.plugins.catalog.refresh_hours` | int | `24` | How old the kept copy of a feed may be before opening the screen reads it again. |
| `workspace.plugins.catalog.release_tokens` | dict[str, str] | `{}` | Read tokens for hosts that keep private packs' release files, by host name, as references (env:NAME or file:/path, never the token itself); sent only to that host when installing. |

Files, in `config/storage.yaml`. A file kind keeps only the media types listed here; the plugin's status notes any it loses.

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `storage.files.max_file_mb` | float | `50` | The largest single file that can be added, in megabytes. |
| `storage.files.max_total_mb` | float | `2000` | The most all added files may take together, in megabytes. |
| `storage.files.accepted_types` | list[str] | `['image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/gif', 'image/webp', 'application/pdf', 'text/plain', 'text/markdown', 'text/csv', 'application/epub+zip', 'font/otf', 'font/ttf', 'font/woff', 'font/woff2', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation']` | Media types a file may have; a file kind can narrow this further. |
| `storage.files.read_max_mb` | float | `25` | The largest file whose text is read, in megabytes. A larger attachment or watched file is named as not read. |
| `storage.files.read_max_chars` | int | `30000` | The most text taken from one file. A file with more is cut there, with a mark saying so. |

## Core records

Plugins read these and refer to them with `RefTo`; they change only through core ops.

### `person` (PER-n)

Someone the workspace works with or tracks. Added by `person.add`; role, org and why_they_matter change through `record.set`; the person edits the rest in the app.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `full_name` | str | required | The name shown wherever the person appears. |
| `first_name` | str \| None | `None` | The name a greeting to them uses, as they write it; empty means the first word of the full name. |
| `aliases` | list[str] | `[]` | Other names that mean this person, such as a first name or nickname. |
| `role` | str \| None | `None` | Their job or part in the work, in plain words. |
| `team` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the team they belong to. |
| `org` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the organization they work for; its name lives on that record. |
| `how_to_reach` | dict[str, str] | `{}` | How to reach them: a channel name mapped to the address or handle for it. |
| `why_they_matter` | str \| None | `None` | Why this person matters to the work, in plain words. |
| `name_verified` | bool | `False` | True when the name's spelling came from the person, a signed header address or a record the person made; false when it was read from outside content and not yet confirmed. |
| `track_only` | bool | `False` | True for someone inside the tracked area who is only observed, not given work. |
| `status` | Literal['active', 'left'] | `'active'` | active: still around. left: no longer part of the work. |

### `organization` (ORG-n)

A company, client, supplier or other body people work for (design 5.1). Its name lives here only: people refer to it by id, so a rename shows everywhere at once.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required | The name shown wherever the organization appears. |
| `aliases` | list[str] | `[]` | Other names that mean this organization. |
| `notes` | str \| None | `None` | Anything worth knowing about it, in plain words. |

### `team` (TEAM-n)

A group of people. The person edits it in the app; no core op changes it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required | The name shown wherever the team appears. |
| `aliases` | list[str] | `[]` | Other names that mean this team. |
| `members` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the people in the team. |

### `project` (PRJ-n)

A piece of work being run, possibly inside another (a book in its series). `project.add` starts one; `record.set` changes status, phase, target, priority, summary, parent and language; `record.log` adds to its log; `project.role` sets a person's part in it; the person edits the rest in the app, and only the person sets its content levels, budget and priority (the assistant's `record.set` of the priority waits for the person).

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required | The name shown wherever the project appears. |
| `group` | str \| None | `None` | The portfolio grouping the project is listed under, from the project-group list. |
| `status` | str \| None | `None` | Where the project stands now, from the project-status list. |
| `phase` | str \| None | `None` | The part of its life the project is in, from the project-phase list. |
| `target` | datetime.date \| None | `None` | The day the project is meant to be finished. |
| `priority` | str \| None | `None` | How important the project is, from the project-priority list. |
| `summary` | str \| None | `None` | A short description of what the project is. |
| `owner` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the person responsible for the project. |
| `links` | list[Link] | `[]` | Pages that belong to the project. |
| `links[].label` | str | required | What the link is, in words for the reader. |
| `links[].url` | str | required | The address to open. |
| `tags` | list[str] | `[]` | Free labels for finding the project. |
| `content_levels` | list[str] | `[]` | Content levels (those defined for AI) its material carries, set by the person; AI work on it goes only to accounts that take them all. |
| `parent` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the project this one belongs to (a book in its series); never itself or below it. |
| `language` | str \| None | `None` | The language tag work on it is written in; unset means its parent's, else the workspace's. |
| `budget_usd` | float \| None | `None` | The most AI work on it and everything in it may cost, set by the person; none for no cap. |
| `log` | list[LogEntry] | `[]` | The update log, oldest first; `record.log` adds a line dated that day. |
| `log[].on` | date | required | The day the line was added. |
| `log[].text` | str | required | What the line says. |
| `roles` | list[ProjectRole] | `[]` | Each person's part in the project (run, design or watch); `project.role` sets one. A person with no entry runs it. |
| `roles[].person` | str | required | The id of the person the role is for. |
| `roles[].role` | Literal['run', 'design', 'watch'] | required | run: they run it. design: they design for it. watch: they only watch it, so the assistant records facts about it and makes no actions or questions for other people. |

### `action` (ACT-n)

Something a person will do. Added by `action.add`, closed by `action.close`, dropped by `action.drop`; `record.set` changes text, due and notes, `action.hold` or the person puts it on hold and the person takes it off, and sending a notice marks who was told. A chase adds a day to `followed_up`; closing records who did the work and who said it was done; dropping records why it is no longer needed and credits no one.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the project it belongs to. |
| `text` | str | required | What is to be done, starting with a verb. |
| `owners` | list[Owner] | `[]` | The people who do it; required unless the action is held. |
| `owners[].person` | str | required | The id of the person who owns the action. |
| `owners[].team` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the team the person acts for here, if any. |
| `due` | datetime.date \| None | `None` | The day it is due. |
| `status` | Literal['held', 'open', 'done', 'dropped'] | `'open'` | held: waiting for an owner to be picked. open: to be done. done: finished. dropped: closed because it is no longer needed; never done, never credited, never chased. |
| `dropped_reason` | str \| None | `None` | Why it was dropped, in plain words; set when it is dropped. |
| `notes` | str \| None | `None` | Extra detail about the action. |
| `on_hold` | OnHold \| None | see below | Set while the action waits for something outside the person's control; the person sets and clears it. An action on hold is never counted as due, overdue or in need of a follow-up, and keeps its due date for when it comes off hold. |
| `on_hold.waiting_for` | str | required | What it waits for, in plain words. |
| `on_hold.since` | date | required | The day it was put on hold. |
| `told` | dict[str, datetime.date] | `{}` | Who has been told about it: a person id mapped to the day they were told. |
| `followed_up` | dict[str, list[datetime.date]] | `{}` | Who has been chased about it: a person id mapped to the days they were chased, oldest first. A chase is not a notice (`told`) and never closes the action. |
| `done_by` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the people who did the work, set when the action is closed. |
| `reported_by` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the person who said it was done, set when the action is closed. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the source it came from, if any. |
| `evidence` | Evidence \| None | see below | The words in the source that justify the action. |
| `evidence.source` | str | required | The id of the source the words come from, or "note" for the person's own note. |
| `evidence.quote` | str | required | The exact words, as they appear in that source. |

### `question` (Q-n)

A question for a person; a decision is a question to the PM. Added by `question.add` or by the engine, closed by `question.done`; the person sends, drops or answers them in the app.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | str | required | The id of the person being asked. |
| `title` | str | required | The question in one line. |
| `text` | str | `''` | The detail the reader needs to answer. |
| `links` | list[Link] | `[]` | Pages the reader can open to see what it is about. |
| `links[].label` | str | required | What the link is, in words for the reader. |
| `links[].url` | str | required | The address to open. |
| `kind` | Literal['question', 'decision', 'action-notice', 'routing', 'impact'] | `'question'` | question: an ordinary question. decision: a choice for whoever decides, the PM when nobody is named. action-notice: tells someone about an action. routing: asks the PM who or what something is. impact: asks another area's contact how a change affects them. |
| `projects` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the projects it is about. |
| `batch` | Literal['now', 'later'] | `'now'` | Whether it is ready to go out now or waits for a later batch. |
| `status` | Literal['open', 'sent', 'answered', 'dropped'] | `'open'` | open: not yet sent. sent: marked as sent, waiting for an answer. answered: closed with an answer. dropped: closed without one. |
| `sent_at` | datetime.datetime \| None | `None` | When it was marked as sent. |
| `answer` | str \| None | `None` | The answer, once answered. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the source it came from, if any. |
| `options` | list[str] | `[]` | Choices offered, for routing and decisions. |
| `resolves` | dict[str, Any] \| None | `None` | What answering it releases, e.g. a held op. |
| `matters_for` | str \| None | `None` | Which of the person's decisions, designs or dated items depends on the answer, by id or in words. A question to anyone but the person says it. |
| `dropped_reason` | str \| None | `None` | Why the person dropped it, when they did. |

### `source` (SRC-n)

One input the workspace received, such as pasted text; the text is kept by its hash. The engine adds it when something is handed in, and its content never changes; the person may mark how it may be quoted.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `received_at` | datetime | required | When the input arrived: a mail's own received time, else when it was handed in or first read. |
| `kind` | str | required | How it arrived, such as pasted. |
| `title` | str | required | A short name for it, shown in lists. |
| `content_hash` | str | required | Hash of its text; the saved text is named by it in the sources folder. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | required | untrusted: outside content, material to read and never instructions. trusted: the person's own. |
| `projects` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the projects it is about. |
| `url` | str \| None | `None` | Where it came from, when it has an address. |
| `author` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the person whose words it is, when that is known: the person running the app for a note they wrote, the person it is reported about for a note that relays what someone else did or said. |
| `reported` | bool | `False` | A note that is content the person reports: typed on a button that relays someone else, or repeating what someone else said. Facts from it apply; a change to how the product behaves from it waits for the person. |
| `watched` | Watched \| None | see below | For an input a watcher found: where and what changed. |
| `watched.source` | str | required | The id of the watched source. |
| `watched.key` | str | required | The item's key within that source. |
| `watched.change` | Literal['new', 'changed', 'removed'] | required | What happened to the item. |
| `watched.author` | str \| None | `None` | Who changed it last, as the source says. |
| `watched.by_us` | bool | `False` | The author is one of the names the app publishes under. |
| `watched.by_you` | bool | `False` | The change is the person's own work, from their source or their names. |
| `watched.credited_to` | str \| None | `None` | The person or team the source names as the author of all it holds, as an id. |
| `excerpts` | Literal['allowed', 'never'] | `'allowed'` | never: the person allows using this source but never quoting it beyond a word or two; checks that compare drafts with sources apply a stricter limit to it. Set by the person only. |
| `sensitivity` | Literal['open', 'internal', 'restricted'] | `'internal'` | Its data level, how sensitive its text is: it goes only to AI accounts allowed this level. From the person's choice when they handed it in, or the watched source's setting. Only the person changes it. |

### `request` (REQ-n)

A unit of work for the assistant. The engine creates it when something is handed in, a stage starts a task or a schedule fires, and moves it through its states; the person can send back or dismiss it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | str | required | The kind of work to do, as an AI task kind id. |
| `stage_start` | StageStart \| None | see below | The stage entry that requested this task. |
| `stage_start.kind` | str | required | The kind of the record that entered the stage. |
| `stage_start.record` | str | required | The id of the record that entered the stage. |
| `stage_start.stage` | str | required | The id of the stage entered. |
| `stage_start.changeset` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the changeset that made the move, if known. |
| `about` | About \| None | see below | The record the work is about, for a task kind that works on one. |
| `about.kind` | str | required | The record's kind. |
| `about.id` | str | required | The record's id. |
| `use` | str \| None | `None` | The account the person picked for this request ("provider/model"), in place of its tier. |
| `approval` | Optional[Literal['required', 'granted']] | `None` | Needs the person's go before dispatch: stage tasks, and runs above the amount to confirm. |
| `estimate_usd` | float \| None | `None` | What the run was estimated to cost when it asked for a go. |
| `note` | str \| None | `None` | The person's own words that came with the request. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the source the request is about, if any. |
| `origin` | Literal['pm', 'input', 'schedule'] | required | Who started it: pm, the person (handing something in or sending work back); input, an outside input; schedule, a schedule or a stage entry. |
| `state` | Literal['queued', 'running', 'review', 'done', 'needs_you', 'failed'] | `'queued'` | queued: waiting its turn. running: with the assistant. review: its changeset awaits the person. done: finished. needs_you: stopped until the person acts. failed: ended with an error. |
| `waiting` | str \| None | `None` | Why it is waiting and until when, in plain words. |
| `cause` | StopCause \| None | see below | Why a request waits, when there is more to it than its words: for one waiting on the person, the cause the screen can offer an action for; for one queued, the time it is waiting for. |
| `cause.kind` | Literal['data_level', 'no_person', 'paused', 'retry', 'offline'] | required | data_level: no AI account may see the request's material, and `accounts` would take it if allowed. no_person: the workspace has no person set yet, so the work waits before any AI call. paused: every account that could take it is waiting for a usage limit to reset (`account`, `until`); the request stays queued and runs again by itself then. retry: a run that gave no usable answer is tried again by itself at `until`. offline: no AI account could be reached for want of a network connection; the request stays queued since `since` and is looked at again at `until`, and no try is counted. |
| `cause.level` | Optional[Literal['open', 'internal', 'restricted']] | `None` | For data_level: the data level of the material. |
| `cause.accounts` | list[str] | `[]` | For data_level: the accounts ("provider/model") that would take the material if allowed its level, in the order the tier tries them. |
| `cause.account` | str \| None | `None` | For paused: the account whose limit resets first. |
| `cause.tier` | str \| None | `None` | For paused: the tier whose work waits. |
| `cause.until` | datetime.datetime \| None | `None` | For paused, retry and offline: when the request runs again by itself. |
| `cause.since` | datetime.datetime \| None | `None` | For offline: when the request first found no network. |
| `follows` | str \| None | `None` | The change (a changeset id) whose event a plugin answered with this work, if any. |
| `sensitivity` | Optional[Literal['open', 'internal', 'restricted']] | `None` | How sensitive the person said what they handed in is; it only ever raises the level. |
| `part` | dict[str, Any] \| None | `None` | The part of a long text the work is about: {first, last} paragraphs (by number) an anchored draft revises or other work reads, or {after} a draft adds new text after (0: at the start; "end": at the end); with the {base} version number they refer to. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | The project the person said a hand-in is about, if they did. |
| `auto_closed` | dict[str, str] \| None | `None` | For a watched change a triage rule closed: {rule, reason}. Taking a closer look clears it. |
| `set_aside` | dict[str, str \| None] \| None | `None` | For a watched mail item set aside as not work: {section, rule, reason}, and for one the person set aside after it was handed in, {from_state, from_waiting} to put it back. It is never queued for the assistant while this is set. This is work clears it. |
| `folded_into` | str \| None | `None` | The newer request this one's change was folded into, so they are read in order, once. |
| `attempts` | int | `0` | How many times the assistant has started on it. |
| `retries` | int | `0` | How many times it was tried again by itself after a run that gave no usable answer. |
| `created_at` | datetime | required | When the request was made. |
| `changeset` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the changeset the assistant proposed for it. |
| `previous` | str \| None | `None` | The request this one redoes after the PM sent it back. |
| `superseded_by` | str \| None | `None` | The later request that redid this one and applied, which retired this attempt: it is done, its held items and open proposals are closed, and nothing is run or shown for it again. |
| `dismissed` | bool | `False` | The PM set this aside without trying again; it no longer counts as needing attention. |
| `dismissed_from` | Optional[Literal['queued', 'running', 'review', 'done', 'needs_you', 'failed']] | `None` | The state the request was in when it was dismissed, put back by undoing the dismissal. |

### `changeset` (CS-n)

What the assistant proposed for one request, how it was checked and what was applied. The applier writes it and updates it on release or undo; the person marks it reviewed.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request` | str | required | The id of the request it answers. |
| `summary` | str | `''` | One line saying what the changeset does. |
| `topic` | str | `''` | A few words naming what the input was about, for the item's title. |
| `ops` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` | One outcome per op: its index, the op, its status (applied, held, refused or undone), group, the records it touched and the reason it was held or refused. |
| `status` | Literal['applied', 'held', 'rejected', 'undone', 'partly_undone'] | required | applied: all ops went through. held: some wait for the person. rejected: set aside. undone: all applied ops were undone. partly_undone: some were. |
| `problems` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` | Problems that belong to the changeset as a whole rather than to one op. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | required | Whether the input it was made from was trusted; records its ops create carry the same mark. |
| `reviewed` | bool | `False` | True once the person has looked at it and accepted it. |
| `run` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the AI run that produced it, if any. |
| `action` | dict[str, Any] \| None | `None` | The person action this came from: its name, target and the choices the person made. |
| `applied` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the knowledge entries the run said it applied, kept only when the run was given them (its knowledge log). A checked citation, never the model's say-so alone. |
| `applied_dropped` | int | `0` | How many ids the run named as applied that it had not been given, which were left out. |
| `missing` | list[str] | `[]` | What the run needed and no op could do, each in a few words, for the weekly missing-op list. |
| `first_on_account` | str \| None | `None` | The name of the AI account when this was the first run on an account that stands in a fallback chain, so its cards can say so. |
| `created_at` | datetime | required | When the changeset was recorded. |

### `fact` (FACT-n)

Something recorded as true, with the words that show it. Added by `fact` and by `question.done`; never edited.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | str | required | The fact, as a statement. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the project it is about, if any. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the source it came from, if any. |
| `evidence` | Evidence \| None | see below | The words that justify it. |
| `evidence.source` | str | required | The id of the source the words come from, or "note" for the person's own note. |
| `evidence.quote` | str | required | The exact words, as they appear in that source. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | `'trusted'` | untrusted when it came from outside content. |
| `key` | bool | `False` | True for the facts that matter most, which are always shown first. |
| `as_of` | datetime.date \| None | `None` | The day the fact was true as of: the day the input it came from was received, unless a later input says otherwise. |
| `supersedes` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the fact this one replaces. The older fact stays on record and is shown as replaced by this one. |
| `basis` | Optional[Literal['person', 'inferred', 'said']] | `None` | Who the fact rests on. person: the person said it. inferred: the assistant worked it out, so it feeds the record only: it never closes anything, never changes a date, an owner or a routing, and never goes on anything others see. said: someone else said it (`said_by`). Empty for a fact recorded before this was kept. |
| `said_by` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the person who said it, when `basis` is said and the input names them. |
| `reaches_children` | bool | `False` | True for a fact about a project that holds for the projects inside it too (a series' fact for each of its books): it goes into the packets of those projects as well. |

### `rule` (RULE-n)

A standing instruction the assistant follows, kept as a record so changing one has history and Undo. The starting set comes from the workspace's rules file; after that the records are the truth. Added by `rule.add` and ended by `rule.retire`.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required | The rule's own name, which stage entry checks and the rules file refer to; never reused. |
| `text` | str | `''` | The rule in the person's wording; it is also its explanation. |
| `applies_to` | Scope | see below | What the rule applies to. |
| `applies_to.task_kinds` | list[str] | `[]` | Task kinds it applies to; empty means all. |
| `applies_to.records` | list[str] | `[]` | Record types or type.field targets it applies to; empty means all. |
| `applies_to.filter` | dict[str, Any] | `{}` | Exact field values narrowing the record targets. |
| `applies_to.projects` | list[Annotated[str, RefTo(kind='project')]] | `[]` | With scope projects, the projects it is for. |
| `applies_to.people` | list[Annotated[str, RefTo(kind='person')]] | `[]` | The people it is about; empty means anyone. |
| `applies_to.scope` | Literal['workspace', 'projects'] | `'workspace'` | workspace: everywhere, except the projects in `except`. projects: only the projects listed in `projects`. |
| `applies_to.except` | list[Annotated[str, RefTo(kind='project')]] | `[]` | With scope workspace, the projects it does not apply to. Dumped by alias, so the key is `except`. |
| `check` | str \| None | `None` | A deterministic check that implements the rule; a rule with none is prose, and prose alone never lets a stage move. |
| `origin` | Literal['seed', 'person', 'input', 'assistant', 'pack', 'import'] | required | Where it came from: seed (the starting set), person (the person's own words), input (content), assistant (its own generalization), pack or import. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | `'trusted'` | untrusted when it was proposed from outside content, until the person keeps it. |
| `status` | Literal['proposed', 'active', 'discarded', 'expired', 'retired'] | `'active'` | proposed: waiting for the person. active: in use. discarded: the person said no. expired: a proposal nobody reviewed in time. retired: it was active and no longer is. |
| `discard_reason` | str \| None | `None` | Why it was discarded: what the person said, or that it was close to one they discarded. |
| `more_evidence` | list[KnowledgeEvidence] | `[]` | What other proposals of the same rule were learned from, merged into this one. |
| `more_evidence[].quote` | str \| None | `None` | The exact words in the source that the entry rests on, as they appear there. |
| `more_evidence[].source` | str \| None | `None` | The input the words come from, when it was saved as one. |
| `more_evidence[].request` | str \| None | `None` | The request whose work produced the entry. |
| `more_evidence[].signal` | str \| None | `None` | The correction the entry was learned from. |
| `more_evidence[].changeset` | str \| None | `None` | The change the correction was about. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | Where it came from, in words. |
| `evidence` | Evidence \| None | see below | The words that justify it, when it came from an input. |
| `evidence.source` | str | required | The id of the source the words come from, or "note" for the person's own note. |
| `evidence.quote` | str | required | The exact words, as they appear in that source. |
| `learned_at` | datetime.datetime \| None | `None` | When the rule was learned or added. |
| `kept_by` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the person who made it active. |
| `kept_at` | datetime.datetime \| None | `None` | When it was made active. |
| `constrains` | list[str] | `[]` | What it is about, so a run's log can tell a rule that applied from one that was only present: op kinds (`question.add`) or op fields (`action.add.owners`). Empty means nothing is checked, so the rule is only ever present. |
| `reviewed_at` | datetime.datetime \| None | `None` | When the person last chose to keep it in a review; the clock for its next review starts here. |

### `event` (EVT-n)

Something dated in the app's own calendar: a day or a moment, or a range of days or moments. Added by `event.add` from what came in, and by plugins and the person later; never written to a calendar service.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|

| `end` | str \| None | `None` | When it ends, in the same forms. Set, it makes a range, and the last day or moment is included. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the project it is about, if any. |
| `source` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the source it came from, if any. |
| `evidence` | Evidence \| None | see below | The words that justify it. |
| `evidence.source` | str | required | The id of the source the words come from, or "note" for the person's own note. |
| `evidence.quote` | str | required | The exact words, as they appear in that source. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | `'trusted'` | untrusted when it came from outside content. |

### `run` (RUN-n)

One call to an AI provider. The engine writes it after each call, for usage and cost reports; nothing changes it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the request the call was made for; none for a call that serves no request (sorting mail headers). |
| `task` | str | required | The kind of task asked. |
| `provider` | str | required | The configured provider that was called. |
| `model` | str | required | The model that answered, as the provider reported it. |
| `tier` | str | required | The configured tier the call was made on. |
| `input_chars` | int | `0` | Characters sent. |
| `output_chars` | int | `0` | Characters received. |
| `input_tokens` | int \| None | `None` | Tokens sent, when the provider reports them. |
| `output_tokens` | int \| None | `None` | Tokens received, when the provider reports them. |
| `cached_input_tokens` | int \| None | `None` | Tokens sent that were read from the provider's cache. |
| `cost_usd` | float \| None | `None` | What the call cost in US dollars; none when it can't be told. |
| `seconds` | float | `0.0` | How long the call took, in seconds. |
| `outcome` | Literal['ok', 'invalid_output', 'error', 'refused'] | required | ok: an answer came back. invalid_output: the answer wasn't in the expected shape. error: the call failed. refused: the provider said it refused the work under its own policy (its reason is in error_detail). |
| `independence` | Optional[Literal['other_account', 'same_account']] | `None` | For a check: other_account, run on an account that didn't write the work; same_account, on one that did, as a fresh run the person accepted. None for other work. |
| `error_kind` | str \| None | `None` | How the call failed, from the runner's own error; none if ok. |
| `error_detail` | str \| None | `None` | The error's own text, for diagnosing a failure. |
| `started_at` | datetime | required | When the call started. |
| `knowledge` | RunKnowledge \| None | see below | What it was given from what was learned, and searched. |
| `knowledge.given` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the knowledge entries and rules it was given. |
| `knowledge.left_out_by_scope` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of rules and entries left out because their scope excludes the input. |
| `knowledge.facts_left_out` | int | `0` | How many facts of the input's projects didn't fit the facts budget. |
| `knowledge.stable_chars` | int | `0` | The size of the knowledge sent with every run, in characters. |
| `knowledge.rules_applied` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the rules it was given that the run's changeset, the check on its output or a later correction shows were applied. Never the model's own claim. |
| `knowledge.rules_present` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the rules it was given that were not shown to apply. |
| `knowledge.rules_moved` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the rules moved out of the always-sent part because it passed its size budget. |
| `knowledge.searches` | list[RunSearch] | `[]` | The searches it asked for. |
| `knowledge.searches[].words` | str | `''` | The words searched for. |
| `knowledge.searches[].kinds` | list[str] | `[]` | The kinds searched: facts, inputs, records, knowledge. |
| `knowledge.searches[].results` | int | `0` | How many results came back. |
| `knowledge.refused_checks` | list[str] | `[]` | The names of the checks that refused this call's answer, each once, including refusals the answer was sent back to fix. |

### `signal` (SIG-n)

A correction by the PM, the measure of how well the assistant does. The engine records one when the person sends work back, undoes it, edits a draft or similar; nothing changes it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | Literal['sent_back', 'undone', 'dropped', 'reworded', 'pulled_back', 'draft_edited', 'held_declined', 'routed', 'set_aside', 'put_on_hold', 'taken_off_hold', 'kept', 'discarded', 'retired', 'narrowed', 'just_this_time', 'change_requested', 'answered_assistant', 'edited', 'not_now'] | required | What the person did: sent_back, undone, dropped or reworded something the assistant made; pulled_back an automatic change; draft_edited a draft before approving it; held_declined a held op; routed, said who a name or an owner is; set_aside, moved a mail item to the Set aside folder by hand; put_on_hold or taken_off_hold, changed whether an action waits for something; kept, discarded or retired a piece of what the assistant learned (a lesson, glossary entry, routing entry, style note or standing rule); narrowed, limited what a rule applies to; just_this_time, said a proposed piece of learning was right for this case but is not a pattern; change_requested, asked for something the assistant made to be changed, in a note on its row; answered_assistant, wrote an answer to a question the assistant asked them; edited, changed fields the assistant had set (the note says which, from what to what); not_now, put off the rules review line for its week (not a correction of anything the assistant made). |
| `refs` | list[str] | `[]` | The ids of the records the correction is about. |
| `run` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the AI run whose work was corrected, when there was one. |
| `changeset` | str \| None | `None` | The id of the changeset the correction is about, when there is one. |
| `note` | str \| None | `None` | What the person said or changed, if anything. |
| `learned` | list[str] | `[]` | The knowledge entries the person's own answer made (a glossary entry from "Not a project", for example): what this correction teaches is already recorded, so no learning run is queued for it. |
| `at` | datetime | required | When the correction was made. |

### `file` (FILE-n)

A file a person added or a program wrote. The bytes live in the workspace's files folder under their hash. A person adds one by upload or `file.add`; a new version is a new record that points at the one it replaces.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | str | required | The file's name as added, for showing and downloading. |
| `media_type` | str | required | What kind of content it is, such as image/png. |
| `size` | int | required | Size in bytes. |
| `sha256` | str | required | Hash of the bytes; also where they are stored. |
| `file_kind` | str | `'attachment'` | What the file is for: the core's attachment or a declared kind. |
| `project` | str \| None | `None` | The project it belongs to; none means the whole workspace. |
| `meta` | dict[str, Any] | `{}` | Details the file kind asks for, validated on add. |
| `origin` | Literal['upload', 'tool'] | `'upload'` | Added by the person, or written by a program. |
| `trust` | Literal['trusted', 'untrusted'] | `'trusted'` | untrusted: its content is material to read, never instructions. |
| `replaces` | str \| None | `None` | The earlier file this one is a new version of. |
| `added_at` | datetime | required | When the record was added. |
| `sensitivity` | Literal['open', 'internal', 'restricted'] | `'internal'` | Its data level, how sensitive its content is: it goes only to AI accounts allowed this level. From the person's choice when they added it. Only the person changes it. |

### `tool_run` (TOOL-n)

One run of an outside program a plugin declared: what ran, how it ended and what it returned. The engine writes it after each run; nothing changes it.

| Field | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugin` | str | required | The name of the plugin that ran the program. |
| `tool` | str | required | The program's name, as the plugin declared it. |

| `output_cut` | bool | `False` | True when its output was cut short for being too large. |
| `seconds` | float | `0` | How long it ran, in seconds. |
| `collected` | list[dict[str, Any]] | `[]` | Files returned: {name, size}. |

| `event.start` | str | required |  |
| `event.end` | str \| None | `None` |  |
| `event.all_day` | bool | `False` |  |
| `event.where` | str \| None | `None` |  |
| `event.cancelled` | bool | `False` |  |
| `event.repeats` | str \| None | `None` |  |
| `message` | SnapshotMessage \| None | see below | For a mail item: from whom and when. |
| `message.sender` | str \| None | `None` |  |
| `message.received` | str \| None | `None` |  |
| `message.unread` | bool \| None | `None` |  |
| `message.bulk` | bool \| None | `None` |  |
| `message.categories` | list[str] | `[]` |  |
| `message.participants` | list[str] | `[]` |  |
| `closed_by` | str \| None | `None` | The triage rule that closed its latest change, so Today leaves it out (a newsletter, say). |
| `set_aside` | dict[str, str] \| None | `None` | For a mail item set aside as not work: {section (personal or sales), rule, reason}, and {confirmed_at} once the person confirmed it (it is then deleted from the app after a short while). Today leaves it out and counts it until it is confirmed; the Set aside folder lists it. |
| `deleted` | bool | `False` | The person confirmed the message was rightly set aside and its content was deleted from the app. Only a marker is kept (the source, key, sender address, date, section and rule), so a later read doesn't hand it in again. |

One read of a watched source and what came of it. The watcher writes it; nothing changes it.
